title: Independent Director
description:
**Operating reality** 

  





 The company coordinates the movement and clearance of customer goods through carriers, gateways, overseas agents, customs\-facing processes and inland service providers. It may advance duties, freight, storage or other charges and later recover them from customers. The enterprise therefore manages documents, instructions, client money, credit, sanctions exposure and time\-critical handoffs without owning every part of the physical journey.
 



 As part of a large unlisted corporate house, the business is formalising governance for sustained international growth. Gross billings can obscure thin collected contribution, unrecovered pass\-through costs, agent balances, demurrage disputes and contingent liability. The Board seeks an Independent Director who can clarify where the company acts as principal, agent, adviser, custodian or payer—and ensure its controls follow the substance of each role.
 



  





**Independent Director remit** 




  





 The appointee will bring rigorous oversight to trade compliance, customs conduct, document integrity, sanctions screening, client funds, overseas agents, shipment profitability, cyber resilience, claims, credit and acquisitions. The Director must be prepared to examine transaction files and exception evidence, not only revenue and shipment counts.
 



  





**Eleven governance priorities** 




  




1. Role clarity in each service.
 
 Define contractual and actual responsibility for booking, documentation, classification, valuation support, duty funding, insurance, custody, subcontracting and delivery. Accounting and liability should follow the real role.
2. Trade and sanctions compliance.
 
 Govern customer, counterparty, goods, route, vessel or conveyance, destination, end\-use and payment screening. Escalation should address ambiguity and attempted circumvention, not only exact database matches.
3. Customs\-facing integrity.
 
 Protect classification, valuation information, origin documents, licences, declarations, inspection handling and record retention. No employee or intermediary may promise outcomes through improper influence.
4. Document and instruction authenticity.
 
 Review authorised customer contacts, change verification, bills and certificates, release instructions, account changes and high\-risk amendments. Email urgency should not override validation.
5. Client\-money protection.
 
 Establish clear ownership, approved accounts, funding evidence, reconciliation, release, unused balance return and prohibition on using one customer's funds for another obligation.
6. Complete shipment economics.
 
 Capture carrier cost, pass\-through charges, agent fees, credit, storage, demurrage, detention, claims, correction effort and receivable days. Gross billing and booked margin should be reconciled to cash realised.
7. Overseas\-agent governance.
 
 Conduct ownership, competence, sanctions, financial, data\-security and conduct diligence. Maintain usable audit, document\-return, incident and transition rights with alternatives for critical locations.
8. Credit and exposure limits.
 
 Aggregate customer exposure across freight, duties, advances, disputes and guarantees. Overrides must be independently approved and immediately visible when ageing or shipment risk deteriorates.
9. Cargo and claims governance.
 
 Define custody points, condition evidence, survey, notification, recovery, insurer coordination and lessons from recurring loss. Claims should not remain outside contract profitability.
10. Cyber and business continuity.
 
 Test fraudulent instruction, account takeover, carrier or gateway outage, document\-system compromise, ransomware, unavailable agents and sudden route closure. Manual processing must preserve authorisation and audit trails.
11. Acquisition and branch control.
 
 Diligence licences, agent balances, customer advances, contingent customs matters, conduct history, claims, systems and owner dependence. Minimum controls must precede revenue synergies.



  





**Decisions reserved for deeper Board challenge** 




  





 The Director will scrutinise entry into new jurisdictions, major customer credit, duty\-funding models, acquisitions, agency partnerships, guarantees, technology changes, controlled\-cargo categories, claims settlements and any arrangement that materially expands principal liability.
 



 Country or gateway expansion should state local legal responsibilities, agent dependence, settlement flows, data handling, compliance competence, working capital and exit options. A high\-volume customer must be assessed on collected contribution and total exposure, not strategic prestige.
 



  





**Audit Committee dashboard** 




  





 The Board should receive gross and net revenue; collected contribution; unreconciled client funds; duty and freight advances; receivable ageing; disputed pass\-through costs; demurrage and detention; agent balances; screening alerts; customs queries; document corrections; cargo claims; cyber incidents; credit overrides; branch exceptions; acquisition remediation; and downside liquidity excluding client money.
 



 Internal audit should trace selected shipments from quote and customer instruction through booking, documentation, screening, clearance, agent settlement, invoice and collection. It should reperformance\-test bank\-detail changes, client\-fund reconciliation, agent due diligence, sanctions escalation, credit overrides and revenue presentation.
 



  





**Candidate credentials** 




  





 Candidates should have at least 25 years of senior leadership across logistics, freight forwarding, shipping, customs, trade finance, banking operations, compliance, audit, finance or multinational service governance. Suitable experience may come from a CEO, CFO, COO, trade\-compliance head, risk officer, gateway leader, Audit Committee Chair or executive responsible for a global agent network.
 



 The candidate must understand transaction\-level risk, cross\-border conduct and working\-capital economics. Experience with client money, sanctions, customs processes, acquisitions, international partners or large family\-controlled corporate houses will be useful.
 



  





**Independence requirements** 




  





 Active inclusion in the
 
 IICA Independent Directors Databank is mandatory
 
 . The candidate must meet an enhanced independence standard appropriate to a large unlisted company. Interests involving promoter entities, customers, carriers, ports or airports, customs intermediaries, overseas agents, banks, insurers, technology vendors, auditors or acquisition targets must be disclosed.
 



 The role may not be used to steer cargo, customers, agents, finance, insurance, technology or advisory assignments toward connected parties.
 



  





**The first 120 days** 




  





 The Director will trace representative high\-risk and high\-value shipments; reconcile client\-money accounts and advances; review customs, sanctions and conduct incidents; test customer and agent concentration on collected contribution; examine recent acquisitions or branches with overdue controls; and establish direct access to compliance, internal audit and whistle\-blower channels.
 



 Within one year, the Board expects clearer principal\-agent boundaries, protected client money, stronger trade screening, realistic shipment profitability, controlled overseas agents and faster closure of customs, claims and receivable exposures.

 This is a high\-impact, product\-facing role for a seasoned banking and finance lawyer who can operate at the intersection of financial services regulation and cutting\-edge technology, ensuring Zeta’s products, partnerships, and client programs are designed and delivered in a manner that is legally sound and regulator\-ready. Reporting into Zeta’s India legal leadership and partnering closely with Product, Compliance, and Risk teams, the role carries significant autonomy and visibility — requiring an individual who can independently own matters end to end, negotiate directly with banks, NBFCs, and technology partners, run and manage a team of capable lawyers, and help shape the legal function of a fast\-growing, high\-growth fintech at the core of India’s digital banking transformation.

* Advise on data privacy, cybersecurity, and data\-localization requirements under the DPDP Act and IT Act, and on legal considerations relevant to maintaining SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications.

title: Head - Legal & Compliance
description:
Head — Legal \& Compliance \| Vantrock Real Assets Private Limited \| Mumbai Metropolitan Region
 



  
 



 Not a general counsel with a department, and not a land\-law seat. One qualified lawyer who commands outside counsel, runs the secretarial calendar for every entity through a small team, and holds the compliance line — for a real assets platform forming a dozen entities and building fast.
 



  
 



 A note before you read on. The team structure, reporting lines, direct reports, seat titles and hiring entity described in this brief reflect the platform's current plan and may change as the platform builds out. Compensation and incentive structures are confirmed in the offer, not here.
 



  
 



 REPORTS TO: Chief Financial Officer · EXPERIENCE: 8–14 years as a qualified lawyer, a meaningful part of it in\-house at a real estate or real\-assets business
 



  
 



 ABOUT VANTROCK
 



 Vantrock is India's independent, operator\-led real assets platform — real assets only — with logistics and industrial as the first phase of its growth.
 



 Founded by Anshul Singhal, Founder \& CEO — three institutional platforms built from zero, the fourth on his own capital; 52 million sq ft delivered (32 million as developer, 20 million as contractor) across his three prior platforms.
 



  
 



 THE FINANCE \& ACCOUNTS TEAM
 



 Vantrock keeps its books in\-house. The finance function owns every number from the site to the board.
 



 Twenty\-one seats when fully built; sixteen live now, one of them already filled. Small enough that every person in it is known by name to the founder; large enough to run a platform properly. Every seat in the team is a builder's seat: the function does not exist yet in the form described here, and the people who join it now are the ones who will decide what it becomes.
 



  
 



 JUDGMENT IN\-HOUSE, DRAFTING OUTSIDE
 



 Vantrock does not run a legal department in the conventional sense, and it does not intend to. Formal opinions come from external firms. Transaction documents are drafted by the counsel retained for the transaction. Litigation, where it arises, is run by litigators. What the platform keeps in\-house is the one thing that cannot be bought by the hour: the person who knows the business well enough to decide what to ask, whom to ask, when the answer is wrong, and when to say no.
 



  
 



 WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
 



 A platform forming a dozen entities, signing construction contracts, taking on lenders, bringing in institutional co\-investors and preparing a fund vehicle generates a volume of legal and secretarial work that cannot be run out of the founder's inbox and a handful of law firms' engagement letters. Today it is. The question of who owns the contract before it goes to counsel, who tracks the ROC calendar across a dozen entities, who tells the founder that a clause he has agreed in principle is a problem — has no answer inside the building.
 



  
 



 WHAT YOU WILL OWN
 



 1\. Corporate legal, commanded. Every contract, transaction, structure and dispute scoped by you before counsel is engaged, briefed by you, reviewed by you before it is signed — and the internal view formed first, so that outside counsel is answering the right question.
 



 2\. The empanelled firms. Choose them, brief them, hold them to fee and quality, and know which firm to use for what.
 



 3\. The secretarial calendar for every entity. Board and partner meetings, resolutions, statutory registers, ROC and LLP filings, annual compliance — for the development company, the investment manager, the sponsor vehicles and every project entity.
 



 4\. The compliance line. A single register of what the group must do, by when, under which law or contract — statutory, regulatory, investor undertakings, with lender covenants mirrored from the corporate finance team's calendar — with an owner and a status against every line, reviewed monthly with the CFO.
 



 5\. Construction and commercial contracts. The platform's standard forms — contractor, consultant, project\-management, lease, facility\-management — built once with counsel and then held, so that the tenth contract is negotiated from the platform's paper, not the counterparty's.
 



 6\. The boundary with land. Working with the investments team's land lawyer so that every land transaction hands over cleanly into an entity, a contract and a filing calendar — with nothing dropped between the two seats.
 



 7\. The team. Recruit, direct and develop the company secretary, the CS\-intermediate and the paralegal; add the second paralegal when volume demands it; and build a seat that a Chief Compliance Officer can be added alongside without a turf line.
 



  
 



 WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
 



 ESSENTIAL
 



 – A qualified lawyer, enrolled with a Bar Council, with 8–14 years in practice — of which a meaningful part in\-house at a real estate developer, an institutional platform, or a business of comparable entity count and contract volume.
 



 – Corporate and commercial law as your core: contracts, entity formation and governance, transactions, employment, the Companies Act and the LLP Act in daily use.
 



 – Having commanded external law firms as the client — scoping, briefing, reviewing, pushing back on the advice and the bill — rather than as the associate drafting for them.
 



 – Company\-secretarial practice understood well enough to supervise it: you know what a filing calendar for a multi\-entity group looks like and what breaks when it slips, even if you have never filed a form yourself.
 



 – Comfortable telling a founder no, in writing, with the reason — and being right often enough to be listened to.
 



 – Based in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, or relocating before joining.
 



 WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT
 



 – Not a general counsel's seat with a large department beneath. The team is a company secretary, a CS\-intermediate and a paralegal. The judgment is yours; the drafting is bought.
 



 – Not a land\-law seat. Title, land acquisition and land litigation belong to the investments team's land lawyer. If land is your first love, that is the seat to look for.
 



  
 



 HOW YOU WILL WORK
 



 – Judgment in\-house, drafting outside. You form the view, then engage counsel; you never engage counsel to form the view.
 



 – Everything runs on the platform's dashboards. The compliance register, the secretarial calendar, the contract library and the panel\-firm scorecard live on the operating layer, not in a private folder.
 



  
 



 COMPENSATION
 



 Vantrock benchmarks compensation against the upper quartile for the role and market, weighted toward equity for candidates who want to build with us long\-term. We discuss specific numbers in the first conversation rather than anchoring either side prematurely.
 



  
 



 CULTURAL FIT
 



 We're building Vantrock over a decade, not a funding cycle. We're looking for people who treat technology as the default answer rather than a supplement, who want to be co\-builders of the platform rather than employees executing instructions, and who are comfortable saying "I don't know" and "I was wrong." If you want a defined role with defined edges, this isn't the right seat. If you want to help build an institution from zero, it might be.
 



 AI proficiency is a standing requirement in every Vantrock seat. You work fluently with AI tools for research, modelling, drafting and analysis, and you build on the platform's dashboards rather than around them. A supervised AI Proficiency Test is part of the process for every seat, at every level of seniority, and we say so openly.
 



 Partner command is the second standing requirement. The books are ours, but auditors, banks, the fund administrator, valuers, law firms and system vendors are commanded by this team — briefed, held to a standard, integrated — never deferred to. We hire for judgment and accountability.
 



  
 



 HOW WE WILL ASSESS
 



 Everyone who applies hears from us within two working days. It carries two links: a fixed set of six questions answered by AI interview — about forty minutes, and the first work sample; we review it before the CV — and the Vantrock AI Proficiency Test, which every hire takes at every level. From there:
 



 1\. The Matter conversation. The matters on your sheet: the one where you overruled outside counsel and were right, the one where you were wrong, and how you built a compliance register the first time. With the CFO — or, until that seat is filled, the Founder \& CEO.
 



 2\. A 90\-minute supervised case. A contractor's standard\-form construction contract with planted problems, and a two\-page group structure — from which you produce the issues note you would send to counsel, the three clauses you would refuse, and the filing calendar the structure implies. Defended to the Founder \& CEO and the CFO once in seat.
 



 Once we have received your application, your AI interview and your test, we will reach out with next steps. Your application is confidential: it is seen only by the Founder's Office and the hiring lead, and nothing is shared with your current employer or referenced without your consent.
 



  
 



 TO APPLY
 



 Write to careers@vantrock.com with the subject line "Head — Legal \& Compliance — \[your name]", and attach:
 



 – Your CV. This is mandatory — a LinkedIn profile alone is not an application; we will read your LinkedIn as well.
 



 – Your Matter Sheet — one row per matter or transaction you led in\-house: type, entities involved, counsel commanded, value or stake in ₹ crore where relevant, year, outcome, your role. The template is available on request. Every row will be discussed.
 



 – Your notice period and what you would need to see to move.
 



 – One short paragraph: the clause that most often gets past a founder in a construction contract, and how you would make sure it never gets past this one. That paragraph matters more than the CV.
 



 We read everything that arrives with a Matter Sheet and a paragraph — properly, not skimmed. If this sounds like your seat, write to us.
 



  
 



 We don't hire roles. We build the platform. · Ownership, not employment. · Builders hire builders.
 




 Founder \& CEO, Vantrock

title: Councel -Land & Transaction - Risk
description:
Counsel — Land \& Transaction Risk \| Vantrock Real Assets Private Limited \| Mumbai Metropolitan Region
 



  
 



 Not a law\-firm seat and not a compliance seat. Every asset this platform buys starts as land, and the founder's own capital goes in first – so title, tenure and approval risk sit with us, not with an investor. This seat controls that risk: it commissions the country's best firms, holds them to the standard and the date, and turns what comes back into a decision.
 



  
 



 ABOUT VANTROCK
 



 Vantrock is an independent real assets platform. Real assets only. We start where we know the ground: logistics, warehousing and industrial parks, across the full chain – first mile, last mile, city\-centre, dark\-store and self\-storage formats, and logistics\-anchored mixed\-use developments with distribution below and office above. From there, in sequence and only as each is delivered: industrial plots; suburban campuses, GCC and back\-office space; strata offices; and, in parallel, data centres and senior living.
 



  
 



 Two decades on this ground and a gap institutional capital left open below the 100\-acre logistics park. The first phase: 10\-to\-50\-acre parcels taken through approvals quickly on the founder's own capital and turned into 2\.5 lakh to 1\.2 million sq ft campuses – shovel\-ready before an investor is ever asked to commit. Pipeline 10 million sq ft; ground breaks on the first 2 million sq ft in January 2027\.
 



  
 



 Three parts, kept deliberately separate. The founder's own balance sheet takes the first risk. Vantrock Real Assets Private Limited – the employer for this seat – is the development manager and operator, with its own board, team and governance. Vantrock Investment Managers LLP is the investment manager; its team underwrites every asset independently and answers to an independent Investment Committee. Assets enter a strategy at cost, with no founder premium, and the platform earns only after its investors have.
 



  
 



 Vantrock was founded by Anshul Singhal, Founder \& CEO, who has built three institutional platforms from zero and is building the fourth on his own capital. 52 million sq ft delivered (32 million as developer, 20 million as contractor), over 2,000 acres acquired, all litigation\-free, more than 200 buildings, and two SEBI Category II funds run to a successful close. Delivered across the founder's three prior platforms. We don't hire roles. We build the platform.
 



  
 



 THE LAND \& INVESTMENTS TEAM
 



 The Land \& Investments team originates, underwrites, structures and closes the land and platform transactions the pipeline is built from, and stays with each asset for its life. The legal function inside it is deliberately two people – a Counsel and a Paralegal. It controls land risk and turnaround across a national pipeline rather than doing the volume work: the country's best land practices do that, and the Big Four advisers do the tax. Judgment, standards, dates and the file stay in\-house.
 



  
 



 THE SEAT
 



 Reports to: Chief Investment Officer / Head of Land \& Investments. Dotted line to the Chief Financial Officer.
 



 Direct reports: Paralegal — Land \& Documentation
 



 Location: Mumbai Metropolitan Region — in person. Substantial travel to NCR, Pune, Bengaluru and to sites, sub\-registrar offices and revenue records wherever a deal sits.
 



 Experience: At least 5 years of relevant land and real estate property law. Total years matter less than those five.
 



  
 



 Team structure, reporting lines, direct reports, seat titles and the hiring entity described here reflect the current plan and may change as the platform builds out. Compensation is confirmed in the offer.
 



  
 



 WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
 



 Every asset this platform buys starts as land, and every land deal carries a legal risk that either gets found before signing or gets paid for afterwards. The founder's own capital goes in first, before any investor is asked to commit, which means title, tenure, encumbrance and approval risk are absorbed by the house and not passed on. This seat is where that risk is controlled.
 



  
 



 The Counsel is not the person who writes the opinion – the country's best land practices do that, and will keep doing it. This seat commissions them, structures the question, holds them to the standard and the date, and translates what comes back into price, structure and whether we proceed. Nobody knows every state's land law and we are not looking for someone who claims to: the record changes name and shape at every border – 7/12 and mutation entries in Maharashtra, Record of Rights and pahani in Karnataka, chitta, adangal and patta in Tamil Nadu, khasra and jamabandi in the north – and what we need is someone who can land in a new state, work out what the record proves, instruct the right counsel and come back with an answer. Resourceful, street\-smart, solution\-minded; the answer is rarely in a textbook.
 



  
 



 WHAT YOU WILL OWN
 



 1\. Own land risk on every live transaction.
 



 2\. Command the firms.
 



 3\. Own the turnaround clock.
 



 4\. Build and hold the gold standard.
 



 5\. Own stamp duty, registration and the tax read.
 



 6\. Read the paper record for what it actually says.
 



 7\. Structure and paper the transaction, then close it.
 



  
 



 TRAVEL IS A REAL AND CENTRAL PART OF THIS SEAT
 



 Not an occasional site visit. Expect to be out of Mumbai a meaningful part of every month, in the states where our deals sit: at the parcel, in revenue and sub\-registrar offices, in local counsel's chambers, and across the table from landowners and their lawyers. Records in India are not fully digital and the risks that matter are rarely the ones already written into a report. If travelling to a tehsil office in a state whose language you do not speak sounds like the wrong kind of work, this is not your seat.
 



  
 



 WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
 



 – At least five years of relevant land and real estate property law. Total years of experience are not the filter; those five are.
 



 – LL.B. from a recognised university, and enrolment with a State Bar Council.
 



 – Hands\-on title diligence on land: chain of title, revenue records, encumbrance, tenure and conversion, litigation search — on deals you personally worked, not supervised from a distance.
 



 – Drafting and negotiating real estate transaction documents: sale deeds, development and joint development agreements, leases and lease deeds, agreements to sell, powers of attorney, conditions precedent and closing documents.
 



 – Experience instructing and managing external counsel — scoping the work, reviewing it, and pushing back when it does not answer the question.
 



 – Working knowledge of land\-related statutes and the approval path for developing land in at least one Indian state — the local record and its vocabulary, tenancy and ceiling history, conversion and land use — and the appetite to learn the next state quickly, on the job.
 



  
 



 What this role is not
 



 – Not a general corporate or compliance seat. Company law, securities and fund compliance sit elsewhere in the group; this seat is land and the transactions built on it.
 



 – Not a litigation seat. Disputes are handled by counsel; you assess what a dispute does to a deal.
 



  
 



 COMPENSATION
 



 Vantrock benchmarks compensation against the upper quartile for the role and market, weighted toward equity for candidates who want to build with us long\-term. We discuss specific numbers in the first conversation rather than anchoring either side prematurely. Wealth creation is part of the engine, not only the salary: performance\-linked bonuses and ESOP\-linked incentives, priced to the seat and confirmed in the offer.
 



  
 



 CULTURAL FIT
 



 We're building Vantrock over a decade, not a funding cycle. We're looking for people who treat technology as the default answer rather than a supplement, who want to be co\-builders of the platform rather than employees executing instructions, and who are comfortable saying "I don't know" and "I was wrong." If you want a defined role with defined edges, this isn't the right seat. If you want to help build an institution from zero, it might be.
 



  
 



 AI proficiency and partner command are standing requirements in every Vantrock seat: you work fluently with AI tools and build on the platform's systems, and you command the institutional partners who execute the transactional work. A supervised AI Proficiency Test is part of the process for every seat, at every level.
 



  
 



 HOW WE WILL ASSESS
 



 One email within two working days of applying, with two links: six fixed questions answered by AI interview – about forty minutes, the first work sample, reviewed before the CV – and the Vantrock AI Proficiency Test. Then: The Land Deal Sheet conversation; A 90\-minute case; Case defence with the Chief Investment Officer / Head of Land \& Investments and the Chief Financial Officer; References. Once we have your application, interview and test, we reach out with next steps. Your application is confidential – seen only by the Founder's Office and the hiring lead, and nothing is shared with your current employer.
 



  
 



 TO APPLY
 



 Write to careers@vantrock.com with the subject line "Counsel — Land \& Transaction Risk — \[your name]", and attach:
 



 – Your CV. This is mandatory — a LinkedIn profile alone is not an application; we will read your LinkedIn as well.
 



 – Your Land Deal Sheet — one row per transaction you have worked on: state and micro\-market, parcel size, transaction type, your role, year, and the principal legal issue you resolved. A simple table is fine; every row will be discussed.
 



 – Your notice period and what you would need to see to move.
 



 – One short paragraph: the single title or tenure issue you would check first on a 30\-acre industrial parcel in a state you have never worked in, and why that one. That paragraph matters more than the CV.
 



  
 



 We read everything that arrives with a Deal Sheet and a paragraph — properly, not skimmed. If this sounds like your seat, write to us.
 



  
 



 We don't hire roles. We build the platform. · Ownership, not employment. · Builders hire builders.
 



  
 



 Founder \& CEO, Vantrock

title: Compliance
description:
**About AlphaGrep Investment Management**
 AlphaGrep Investment Management Private Limited (AlphaGrep IM) is a Quantitative Investment Management firm offering regulated funds, Portfolio Management Services (PMS), Alternative Investment Funds (AIF), and Investment Advisory services to domestic and global clients.
   

  

 AlphaGrep IM is the brainchild of the team at AlphaGrep, a SEBI\-regulated broker and multi\-asset proprietary trading firm focused on quantitative trading across more than 20 global exchanges.
   

  

 We are looking for a bright and resourceful individual to join our
 **Compliance team in Mumbai**

 **Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), Portfolio Management Services (PMS), and Investment Advisory (IA)** 
 businesses.
   

  

 The ideal candidate should have strong practical knowledge of SEBI regulations applicable to AIF, PMS and Investment Advisers, with the ability to independently identify regulatory requirements and translate them into actionable compliance processes.
   

  

 Key Responsibilities

* Monitor PMS client onboarding, agreements, investment mandates, disclosures and applicable regulatory requirements.

* Review regulatory submissions for accuracy, completeness and consistency.
* Coordinate with Operations, Finance, Fund Accounting, Legal and other teams for information required for regulatory reporting.
* Maintain a repository of regulatory filings, acknowledgements and supporting documents.

* Draft, review and periodically update compliance policies, SOPs and internal controls applicable to AIF, PMS and Investment Advisory.

* Monitor screening, sanctions/PEP checks, adverse media and other AML controls.
* Escalate and document AML/KYC exceptions and suspicious activities in accordance with applicable requirements.

 Qualification

**Experience**
* 3–5 years of relevant experience in Compliance, Legal \& Compliance or Regulatory Compliance.

* Strong practical understanding of SEBI regulations applicable to AIF, PMS and Investment Advisers.

 Chief Financial Officer /Board of Directors / Managing Director

 : Panorama Studios International Limited.
 




**Company Website** 

 : https://panoramastudios.in/
 




  




**Role overview:** 


 The Company Secretary will serve as a vital link between the Company, its Board of Directors, shareholders, government and regulatory authorities. The primary responsibility is to independently ensure absolute compliance (SEBI \& Listing Regulations), secretarial works with all relevant statutory and regulatory requirements, particularly focusing on SEBI regulations and the Companies Act, while maintaining the highest standards of corporate governance.
 




  




**Key Responsibilities** 
**1\. Board \& Committee Management** 
* Schedule, organize, and conduct Board meetings, Committee meetings, and General Meetings (AGMs/EGMs).
* Formulate agendas, prepare comprehensive board notes, and draft precise minutes of the meetings.
* Ensure timely implementation of and follow\-up on decisions taken by the Board.



  




**2\. SEBI \& Listing Compliances** 
* **SEBI (LODR) Regulations:** 

 Manage continuous and periodic disclosures, financial result submissions, corporate governance reports, and event\-based intimations to stock exchanges (BSE \& NSE).
* **SEBI (PIT) Regulations:** 

 Maintain the Structured Digital Database (SDD), manage the closure of trading windows, and track disclosures related to insider trading.
* **SEBI (SAST) Regulations:** 

 Monitor shareholding patterns and ensure timely disclosures regarding the acquisition and takeover of shares.
* **SEBI (ICDR) Regulations:** 

 Handle compliances related to further capital issuance, preferential issues, or rights issues if undertaken by the company.
* Updated management about the latest amendment and their compliance.



  




**3\. Corporate Law \& Statutory Compliances** 
* Ensure absolute compliance with the
 
**Companies Act, 2013** 

 and the rules made thereunder.
* File necessary e\-forms, returns, and financial statements with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) / Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA).
* Maintain all statutory registers, books, and records as required by law.
* Oversee compliance with the
 
**Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act (SCRA)** 

 and the
 
**Depositories Act** 

 regarding dematerialization and transfer of securities.



  




**4\. Shareholder \& Stakeholder Relations** 
* Coordinate with the Registrar and Share Transfer Agent (RTA) to resolve investor grievances efficiently.
* Manage corporate actions such as dividend declarations, bonus issues, or stock splits.

 Associate/Fellow Member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI).

 Strictly
 
**5 years of post\-qualification experience** 

 working actively within a company listed on the BSE and/or NSE.
* *Preferred:* 

 An additional degree in Law (LL.B.) will be highly advantageous.



  




**2\. Core Legal \& Regulatory Knowledge** 


 The ideal candidate must possess deep working knowledge and practical hands\-on experience in:
 



* Companies Act, 2013 \& Rules
* SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations \[LODR]
* SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations \[PIT]
* SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations \[SAST]
* SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations \[ICDR]
* SEBI Act, Depository Act, and SCRA



  




**3\. Skills \& Competencies** 
* **Drafting Skills:** 

 Exceptional ability to draft board resolutions, minutes, annual reports, and legal notices.
* **Communication:** 

 Strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively interact with Board Members, Regulators, and Legal Counsel.
* **Attention to Detail:** 

 Meticulous approach to tracking compliance deadlines to ensure zero\-penalty operations.
* **Integrity:** 

 High ethical standards, confidentiality, and professional maturity.

 hr@panoramastudios.in
 
 along with their Current CTC, Expected CTC and  Notice Period.

title: Director - Group Company Secretary
description:
**Group Company Secretary \& Head – Global Governance**
**The CoinDCX Journey: Building the Future of Finance**
 At CoinDCX, our mission is clear \- to make crypto and blockchain accessible to every Indian and enable them to participate in the future of finance.
   

  

 As India’s first crypto unicorn valued at $2\.45B, we are reshaping the financial ecosystem by building safe, transparent, and scalable products that power adoption at scale.
   

  

 We believe that change starts together. It begins with bold ideas, relentless execution and people who want to build what’s next.
   

  

 If you’re driven by purpose and thrive in environments where your work defines the next chapter of an industry, you’ll feel right at home here.
   

  

**About The Role**
 This isn’t a typical Company Secretary role.
   

  

 You will serve as the
 **governance backbone of CoinDCX’s global entity structure** 
 , ensuring statutory compliance, board governance, and regulatory discipline across India, Dubai, Mauritius, Jordan, and any future jurisdictions.
   

  

 This role exists to build and safeguard the company’s governance architecture as we scale globally in a highly regulated industry. You will act as the custodian of global compliance standards across Finance, HR, Compliance, and Legal functions, ensuring our governance framework is robust, audit\-ready, and aligned with potential future listing requirements.
   

  

 You will work closely with the CFO, Legal, Compliance, Board members, and external advisors to drive best\-in\-class governance standards across all entities.
   

  

**What You’ll Do**
* Lead global corporate governance across all CoinDCX entities, ensuring statutory compliance and governance alignment across jurisdictions.
* Own and manage Board \& Committee processes , including agendas, minutes, resolutions, regulatory disclosures, and action trackers.
* Drive compliance under the Companies Act, FEMA, and relevant international regulations , coordinating with local advisors in UAE, Mauritius, Jordan, and other geographies.
* Act as the cross\-functional compliance custodian , ensuring HR, Finance, and Compliance teams meet statutory obligations and governance standards.
* Strengthen IPO and capital markets readiness , building board structures, documentation systems, and compliance processes aligned with public market norms.
* Oversee ESOP governance, cap table management, and share allotments , ensuring transparency and regulatory adherence.
* Develop and refine corporate governance policies , including delegation matrices, board charters, and internal compliance frameworks.


**You’ll Excel in This Role If You**
* Think in systems and build governance frameworks that scale with complexity.
* Have deep expertise in Companies Act compliance and multi\-entity structures with more than 10 years of experience.
* Are calm, structured, and decisive in high\-stakes regulatory environments.
* Communicate with clarity and confidence at Board and CXO levels.
* Bring global perspective while executing with operational precision.
* Have experience in listed public companies or IPO\-readiness environments.
* Thrive in regulated, fast\-evolving industries like fintech or crypto.


**You’ll Know You’re Winning When**
* All group entities operate with zero material compliance lapses.
* Board meetings run with precision, structure, and complete documentation.
* Secretarial audits are completed smoothly with clean observations.
* Cross\-functional compliance trackers are institutionalized and automated.
* Governance standards are aligned with IPO and public\-market expectations.
* Leadership and auditors view the governance function as proactive and strategic, not reactive.


**Why This Role Matters \& What’s In It For You**
 This role is central to CoinDCX’s long\-term credibility and scalability. As a regulated, global fintech company, governance is not a support function — it is a strategic pillar.
   

  

 You will work closely with senior leadership, influence high\-stakes structural decisions, and help shape the governance architecture of one of India’s most trusted crypto platforms. This is an opportunity to operate at the intersection of compliance, capital markets, and global scale.
   

  

**Hiring Process**
 Here’s what your journey with us looks like:
   

  

 Application Review – We assess for skills, alignment, and intent
   

  

 Recruiter Connect – A short conversation to understand you better
   

  

 Functional Round(s) – Deep dive into governance expertise, global compliance experience, and real\-case scenarios
   

  

 Assignment / Simulation Round – A practical exercise involving governance structuring or compliance case evaluation
   

  

 Culture \& Values Discussion – A conversation to understand our ways of working and how you thrive best
   

  

 Founder Conversation (Optional) – For senior leadership alignment and strategic discussion
   

  

**Where We Work**
 We believe the best ideas emerge when people build together. Collaboration, speed and trust come alive when teams share the same space.
   

  

 With this belief, we operate as a work\-from\-office organisation. This role is based out of our
 **Mumbai office** 
 , where governance, leadership alignment, and execution move in real time.
   

  

**Perks That Empower You**
 We believe great people deserve great experiences.
   

  

 Design Your Own Benefits: Flexible perks to match your lifestyle
   

  

 Unlimited Wellness Leaves: Rest and recharge as you need
   

  

 Mental Wellness Support: Access to therapy and wellness resources
   

  

 Learning Sessions: Bi\-weekly learning and growth opportunities
   

  

**Ready to Build What’s Next?**
 If you’re looking for a role that gives you direct access to high\-stakes governance decisions, deep impact across global entities, and a chance to strengthen the foundation of India’s leading crypto platform, this is it.
   

  

 Join CoinDCX and help us build the future of finance — responsibly, globally, and together.

description:
**Who we are**





 As a global law firm our work spans jurisdictions, cultures, and languages – and so do our people.

 You’ll build connections and work with colleagues as one global team. You’ll unlock opportunities for clients, across borders, cultures, legal and commercial disciplines.
   

  





 Join us to work with colleagues as one global team – empowering each other to be exceptional and create advantage for our clients.
   

  





 Our India team is a well\-established and integral part of the firm’s global operations, delivering high\-value support across a wide spectrum of functions. With over 800 business professionals based in Gurugram and Hyderabad, we’ve been driving operational excellence and innovation for more than 15 years.
   

  





 We contribute to global success in areas such as Information Technology, Finance, Human Resources, Risk \& Compliance, Legal Support, Research \& Knowledge, Document Production, Virtual Executive Assistance, Programme Management, Client \& Market Development, and Continuous Improvement.
   

  

  

  

  

  




**Job Description**


**The role**





 The Clearance Centre is a central part of the firm's risk management function and reports ultimately to the firm's General Counsel.
   

  

  

  






**Who you will work with**





 Working within the Post Clearance Team ("PCT") in CC Delhi, you will be part of a team responsible for the management of conflicts of interest and associated compliance issues across Clifford Chance's global practice, including Europe, the Middle East and Asia. Your primary responsibility will be making decisions on whether new mandates can be accepted or the scope of existing matters amended in the context of current conflicts and regulatory rules, and internal firm policies.
   

  

  

  






**What you will be responsible for**





 The fundamental responsibility of the role is to review requests for clearance to amend existing matters, open supplementary matters and liaise with partners and other fee earners to determine the appropriate ways to do this.
   

  





 In addition, you will undergo extensive ongoing training on:
   

  




* UK conflicts rules and their application in practice;
* Clearance Centre processes and procedures;
* Risk and compliance policies;
* Matter intake workflows




**What you will do**




* Develop comprehensive knowledge of CC conflict policies and their application to real situations as needed.
* Perform initial review of submissions from matter teams and evaluate accuracy and appropriateness of requests.
* Analysing information contained in the Firm's conflict management systems.
* Perform research on various databases to understand the relationship with client and counterparties involved in the new proposal and identify any potential conflicts of interest that may arise.
* Perform research on external databases like Orbis and Merger market to find information about various entities involved in an engagement.
* Assist and analyse for existing mandates whether the updated scope of work is in line with original scope of work cleared on the matter.
* Monitoring mailboxes and responding to the requests of Global and local teams of the firm.
* Facilitate and drive the process to completion by following up on requests from fee earners/secretaries.
* Escalate complex requests to the senior team members.


**Qualifications**


**Your experience**




* Any Graduate, Law degree and legal qualification preferred;
* Minimum 3\-4 yrs of work experience in a corporate/MNC;
* Experience in using Intapp Open or similar tool;
* Experience and ability to work well with others as part of a team and to also work independently;
* Some experience of working in a commercial environment (legal or otherwise) would be very useful, but not essential;
* Analytical skills and a proven ability to solve problems in a methodical and practical way;

title: Chief Compliance Officer
description:
Own the compliance function end to end and build it from the ground up. This role holds the board\-approved digital lending policy, the regulatory calendar, and the organisation's relationship with the regulator. It is a build mandate, not a maintenance one — you will be defining what compliance looks like here before anyone else does.
 



**Key Responsibilities** 




 ● Draft, obtain board approval for, and maintain the digital lending policy and Fair Practices Code.
 



 ● Own registration and upkeep of all Digital Lending Apps on the RBI CIMS portal.
 



 ● Build and run the Lending Service Provider due diligence and ongoing oversight framework, including periodic audits.
 



 ● Own the compliance calendar — periodic returns, statutory audits, certifications and board reporting.
 



 ● Ensure Key Fact Statement discipline and disclosure accuracy across every product and channel.
 



 ● Manage regulatory correspondence, inspections and any remediation arising from them.
 



 ● Advise product, credit and technology teams on regulatory impact before launch, not after.
 



**Requirements** 




 ● 10–15 years in regulatory compliance at an NBFC, bank, digital lender or payment institution.
 



 ● Direct hands\-on involvement in an RBI inspection, an NBFC licensing process, or implementation of the 2025 Digital Lending Directions — the application must state which.
 



 ● Working knowledge of Scale Based Regulation, outsourcing norms and Fair Practices Code.
 



 ● CS, LLB or CA preferred.
 



 ● Ability to write policy that survives regulatory scrutiny and to say no to the business when required

title: GDS GCO Enablement Team - Senior Associate - CC Team
description:
At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.
   

  

**Job Title**
**Senior Associate \- Commercial Contracting**
**Service Line/Sub\-Business Line**
 Legal
   

  

**Qualification**
 LL. B (professional qualification)
   

  

**The opportunity**
 This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast\-growing team within EY. Part of the GDS GCO Enablement team in India, the counsel will work with legal/Global General Counsel’s Office (GCO) attorneys, and support EY’s business on client and vendor contracts. You will provide legal support to the business and become a trusted adviser of stakeholders (often at senior leadership level). You will be expected to assess and understand how risks can be best managed and mitigated
   

  

**Your Responsibilities**
**Key responsibilities will include the following:**
* Drafting, reviewing, negotiation, finalization and advisory on vendor agreements (including statements of work and terms \& conditions), Service agreements, framework agreements, proposals, sponsorship contracts, meeting, collaboration agreements and event agreements, Speaker services agreement, and other ancillary documentation, ad\-hoc projects providing risk management advice in relation to each of them.
* Act as point of contact for EY’s business/procurement teams and support the legal team.
* Have a good understanding of general key business risks that need to be managed (training will be facilitated in respect of EY’s specific risk management framework)
* Assist with trainings to new joiners and junior team members.
* Coordinating with internal specialist functions including Independence, onshore legal teams, Security, Privacy and Risk Management
* Maintaining an understanding of the impact of changes in EY policies, organizational structure, and procedures.


**Skills And Attributes For Success**
 You will be provided with training and coaching on the job.
   

  

**We are looking for someone who has the following attributes and skills:**
* Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively communicate with internal stakeholders and vendors;
* Ability to team effectively with onshore legal team and colleagues in other functions;
* Ability to grasp, understand, and accurately articulate and document the transactions;
* Ability to assess size, scope and overall risk of contemplated transactions and to tailor contracts accordingly;
* Highly responsive with ability to manage high workload volumes efficiently and effectively;
* Solution oriented with focus on exceptional client service;
* Keen attention to detail;
* Strong communication and English language (verbal and written) skills;
* Confidence, maturity and high degree of awareness to be able to work effectively with a broad base of senior\-level internal stakeholders;
* Strong service\-oriented personality, proficient at delivering the highest quality of work within deadlines.
* High levels of personal energy and appetite for work and success.


**Experience And Qualifications**
* Law Graduate/LL.B, with 3\-5 years of relevant post\-qualification experience in contract review, drafting and negotiation experience;
* Knowledge of data protection (GDPR/CCPA), privacy and security terms
* Understanding of compliance related concepts such as Independence, Conflicts.
* Experiences in drafting and negotiating IP terms in contracts


**What We Look For**
 Someone who wants to grow into a new role at EY and develop new skills and attributes
   

  

 A passion to contribute to the growth of the wider GCO and GDS team
   

  

**What Working At EY Offers**
 EY Global Delivery Services (GDS) is a dynamic and truly global delivery network. We work across five countries – Argentina, China, India, the Philippines, Spain and Poland – and with teams from all EY service lines, geographies and sectors, playing a vital role in the delivery of the EY growth strategy. From accountants to coders, we offer a wide variety of fulfilling career opportunities that span all business disciplines. In GDS, you will collaborate with EY teams on exciting projects and work with well\-known brands from across the globe. We’ll introduce you to an ever\-expanding ecosystem of people, learning, skills and insights that will stay with you throughout your career.
   

  

**EY \| Building a better working world**
 EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long\-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets.
   

  

 Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.
   

  

 Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

title: Senior Compliance Manager
description:
**About Policybazaar.com –**




 PolicyBazaar.com is India's leading digital insurance marketplace and one of the most valuable insur\-tech companies globally. We started our journey in 2008; in 2018 we became just the third Unicorn in India and went public in 2021\.
 



  





 Policybazaar is at heart a data and technology company that has revolutionized the insurance market in India.
 



 We deploy cutting edge technology, use advanced data analytics and leverage AI/ML to offer customer centric
 



 products, optimized customer journeys, and ensure superior customer experience across the insurance value
 



 chain. We have had a major influence on how protection insurance products are bought in the country and are
 



 responsible for sourcing a significant portion of the market in Term and Health insurance.
 



 In FY25, we sourced over 23\.5K Crores of Premium and have been growing at \~44% CAGR for the last five years.
 



 We have 10cr\+ registered users and have provided insurance to 2cr\+ people. We have an industry leading 93%
 



 market share of the online aggregator market.
 



  





 Brands under the PB Fintech Umbrella: Paisabazaar.com, Policybazaar For Business, PB Partners, Policybazaar
 



 Visit policybazaar.com to know more about us.
 



  





**Role Overview:**




 Job Role: Manager/ Senior Manager Compliance
 



 Location\- Gurugram, Haryana
 



 Experience\- 6\-8 Years
 



  





**Role and Responsibilities:**




 1\. End to end compliance management and ensuring a compliance culture in the organization.
 



 2\. Keeping track of all regulatory changes/laws impacting the business of the company. Ensuring trackers are updated, new
 



 requirements are implemented in the Company and the requirements are continuously tracked through the compliance
 



 tool.
 



 3\. Responsible for assisting in regulatory / legal compliances along with regulatory and statutory audits on need basis.
 



 4\. Conducting compliance reviews of critical areas and preparing a report along with the remediation plan.
 



  





**Other Responsibility Areas \-**




 1\. End to end contract management (vetting, negotiating and execution of agreements including strategic agreements).
 



 2\. Maintenance and regular review of all executed agreements with renewal follow\-ups with business.
 



 3\. Periodic review and ensuring legal compliance of company’s website.
 



 4\. Maintaining good co\-ordination with all internal departments of the company and liaise with external counsels for
 



 regulatory work as and when required.
 



 5\. Other tasks that may be specified from time to time.
 



  





**Requirements and skills \-**




 1\. Law degree from a reputed college / university.
 



 2\. Post qualification experience of 6 to 8 years working in regulatory compliance departments of corporates / law firm.
 



 Experience of working in the regulatory compliance department of fin tech companies will be an added advantage.
 



 3\. Excellent knowledge and understanding of corporate law and procedures. Knowledge of insurance / SEBI / RBI regulations
 



 will be an added advantage.
 



 4\. Sound legal reasoning with an ability to create legal defensive or proactive strategies.
 



 5\. Outstanding communication skills, self\-starter with an ability to meet deadlines in a competitive environment.

title: Compliance Business Partner
description:
**About Olympus** 




 Olympus Medical Systems India Private Limited (Olympus) commenced its business operation in Indian market on April 1, 2010\. Olympus is a wholly owned subsidiary of Olympus Corporation, which expanded globally into the Indian market, among others, with the aim of being the most respected reliable and chosen brand in the healthcare domain. Olympus established its direct presence to build very strong marketing and service facilities. With better and innovative technology, Olympus looks forward to expanding its foothold in the market in tandem with the growth in Indian economy. In addition, the Group is in the process of establishing a separate legal entity in Hyderabad, India, known as Olympus Technology Centre India (OTCI). This new entity represents a strategic investment in expanding Olympus' research and development capabilities in India, with the aim of diversifying innovation activities and accelerating advancements in medical technology.
 



**Business Overview** 




 Olympus has a wide portfolio of products with the latest innovative and superior technology. Olympus deals primarily in two verticals, i.e. Gastrointestinal Solutions Division (GIS) and Surgical \& Interventional Solutions Division (SIS), and contributes to medical advancement in society with its state\-of\-the\-art products. Olympus also has a wide range of Scientific Solutions Products for the non\-medical segment in India.
 



 Role Overview
 



 Core objective of this role is to provide support on compliance matters for Olympus business throughout India and in the near future, compliance matters of OTCI. The selected candidate is expected to work closely with all internal stakeholders and the regional Compliance team in ensuring that compliance risks in India are managed appropriately and consistently.
 



 Key Responsibilities
 



 •Lead the development, implementation and maintenance of a Compliance programme.
 



 •Be a part of Olympus executive leadership team and provide strategic direction on Compliance and ethics.
 



 •Drive Compliance awareness in the organization and provide guidance to colleagues.
 



 •Provide day\-to\-day guidance and support on Compliance matters to all business units and functions.
 



 •Support and coordinate employee compliance with the Global Code of Conduct and related Compliance policies.
 



 •Coordinate and attend Compliance Committee meetings.
 



 •Partner with Governance functions, HR, Finance and other divisions.
 



 •Coordinate with APAC and Global Compliance Divisions and communicate progress to management.
 



 •Ensure compliance with applicable Indian laws, regulations, industry codes, and company policies, including anti\-bribery, anti\-corruption, competition law, data privacy, and healthcare compliance requirements.
 



 •Oversee third\-party compliance due diligence processes
 



 •Advise business leaders on compliance risks associated with commercial initiatives, tenders, sponsorships, grants, donations, and healthcare professional engagements.
 



 •Support internal and external audits and coordinate remediation plans for identified compliance gaps.
 



**Minimum Requirements** 




**Qualification:** 




 Degree in law or related field.
 



**Professional Experience:** 




 At least
 **15 years experience** 
 in Compliance or a related field, including experience in a corporate organization.
 



 Preferred: Professional certification as a Certified Compliance \& Ethics Professional, Professional Risk Manager or equivalent.
 



**Competencies** 




 •Integrity and professional ethics
 



 •Familiarity with the Uniform Code for Marketing Practices in Medical Devices (UCMPMD), industry practices and professional standards
 



 •Knowledge of risk assessment and control
 



 •Attention to detail
 



 •Business Acumen
 



 •Customer focus
 



 •Execution Excellence
 



 •Domain Expertise
 



 •Communication
 



 •Developing Organizational Talent
 



 •Team Leadership

title: Commercial Contract Analyst
description:
Job Description
 







 At Inizio,
 
 we value inclusivity, recognize the power of diversity, and inspire the next generation of change\-makers. We are an equal opportunities employer. We believe in creating a work environment that values diversity, equity, and inclusion. We strive to recruit from a diverse slate of candidates and foster an environment that provides the right conditions for long\-term success. We welcome all applications regardless of race, colour, religion or belief, gender, gender identity, age, national origin, marital status, military veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation and physical or mental disability.
 




**The Role** 





 The Contract Analyst is responsible for managing client contracts and building relationships both with our clients and across the business.
 



 This position is business partnering with one of our Business Units.
 



 This is a hybrid working role reporting to a Commercial Affairs Manager.
 



**Key Responsibilities** 




 Business Partnering
 


* Foster excellent relationships with internal stakeholders.
* Provides regular status updates.



 Contract Management
 


* Collaborate with legal and agency teams to draft, review, and finalize contracts with clients in a timely manner.
* Ensures contracts meet quality and commercial standards.


* Manages the contract lifecycle using the HighQ system ensuring contracts repository is kept up to date.
* Supports business and clients with contracting questions


* Understands key operational and financial drivers of allocated Business Unit
* Works simultaneously on multiple contracts and contract amendments



 Business Metrics
 


* Track, manage and improve contract related metrics that demonstrate customer service.



 Relationship Management
 


* Build and maintain strong relationships with clients and business partners to ensure customer satisfaction and foster long\-term collaborations.



 Problem Solving
 


* Analyse information to solve problems and present proposed solutions to Management with Manager support.



 Communication and Negotiation
 


* Demonstrate strong communication and negotiation skills in engagements with internal teams and external clients.
* Effectively convey complex information and negotiate deals that align with the company's objectives.



**What skills and experience you bring to the role** 




* Keen eye for detail
* Excellent organizational, negotiation and communication skills
* Ability to solve problems, analyse information and achieve quality standards
* Good understanding of contract language
* Good analytical skills.
* Flexible and able to operate in a dynamic, fast paced environment
* Minimum of a bachelor’s level degree
* Proven experience in a commercial affairs / contracting role. Some background in working with Life Sciences / Pharmaceutical industry is preferable



**Who are Inizio?** 





 We help our clients navigate their clinical development and commercialization journey by connecting the best scientific knowledge, market intelligence, actionable data, technology, communication, and creative execution.
 



 With a global presence and multiple career paths, the career possibilities are expanding at Inizio. We’re a growing global team of 11,700 \- a $1\.5bn revenue business working with the world’s leading health and life sciences businesses, and we have exciting growth plans. Whoever and wherever you are, we’ll empower you with the autonomy you need to experiment, learn, and grow. We’ll make sure that you feel valued, supported and, of course, because we’re helping our clients to transform healthcare and improve millions of lives you can feel pride in your work at Inizio.
 






*Don't meet every job requirement? That's okay! Our company is dedicated to building an inclusive and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role, but your experience doesn't perfectly fit every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this role or others.*

title: Contract Management Spec
description:
**Job Description**
**Job Overview:**
 The Contracts Management Specialist manages and delivers Contracts Management activities across global projects utilizing existing practices to resolve routine and moderately complex commercial issues while ensuring alignment with contractual obligations.
   

  

 They are required to take ownership of contracts administration across all project phases, working with guidance and direction from seniors within the team, while proactively coordinating with multi\-disciplinary teams on large scale projects.
   

  

 The role offers continued professional growth through hands\-on project involvement, exposure to complex contractual scenarios, and opportunities for advanced development and training within the contracts management discipline
   

  

**Responsibilities**
**Key Tasks and Responsibilities:**
* Drive the on\-time delivery of the projects that McDermott execute.
* Independently support the Contracts Management team of various projects on contract related matters, escalating critical issues appropriately.
* Implementing procedural requirements relevant to project contracts management – ensuring contractual compliance and project adherence to relevant contractual procedures.
* Documentation control, compliance tracking and reporting.
* Support in the development of material for the overall Contracts Management organization, including material for the centralized Portal to serve as a central repository for the global organization working on projects worldwide,
* Ensure maintenance of data schedules, contract records and support in reporting requirements.
* Record contractual correspondence and draft notices – coordinate with project management and other disciplines to ascertain facts and supporting information.
* Develop dashboards, reports and KPIs related to contractual performance
* Contribute to in pre\-contract activities to support in development of projects prior to award.
* Identifying, assessing, reviewing, and reporting contractual risks for individual items under the project contracts.
* Coordinate Change management, Claims and Disputes (evaluation of schedule and cost impacts, coordination and documentation).
* Review and monitor subcontractors and suppliers contractual compliance, documentation and records.
* Manage contractual communications with Vendors and Subcontractors
* Develop interface relationships with project supply chains and the interlinks between various contracts/subcontracts.


**Qualifications**
**Essential Qualifications and Education:**
* Bachelor's / Post Graduate Degree with background in Contract Management, Quantity Surveying, Construction Management or Engineering.
* It is preferable to have five to eight (5\-8\) years exposure of working experience in Contracts Management or similar experience and roles in EPC energy or infrastructure projects, construction or subcontract management.
